address: Warmoesstraat 157-163, Amsterdam: 1981 perforated-brick car park with a stone-and-brick wing at its north end
notes: Warmoesstraat 157-163 (BAG), built 1981: the Beurs-quarter car park. A 32 m block clad in a perforated brown brick screen (square grid of open and glass-block cells over bare concrete decks), curved on its Warmoesstraat end where a casino (PLAYERS) fills the glazed ground floor; a stone-based brick wing with tall timber windows closes the north-east end; a blue-glass cylinder stands behind (2025 panorama w02-130).

Modelled: the screen as brick-bay-grid with wide low windows (7 decks, 8 bays: the perforation grid reads as a window field, not as 1 m open cells), the SE podium (4 decks), the stone-and-brick wing with 4 storeys x 4 bays and a cornice. Walls without a photograph and the large NW party walls stay blank. The 49 m SE wall (panel 30) carries the blue-glass cylinder: its eaves (23.5 m) do not match the lower LoD2.2 roof behind it (19.3 m), so no group may own it and it stays blank. Not modelled: the PLAYERS lettering, the curved glazed casino ground floor, the car-park ramps and gate, the stone plinth of the wing.

Components lane (2026-10-13): walls[0]-[2] are now the perforated-brick screen (screen: true): a concrete lattice of posts at every bay joint and rails at every deck line (w01-136, w06-312: cells about 1.5 m wide, one deck tall), with glass-block perforations in one bay of three, staggered per deck. Bays re-counted to the lattice: 32 on walls[0], 10 on walls[1], 18 on walls[2]. Simplified: the glass-block clusters are scattered by a fixed stagger, not placed cell by cell from the photograph; the thin cross ribs inside each lattice cell are not modelled.
